question.text: An earthen pitcher loses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of water per minute due to evaporation. If the water equivalent of pitcher is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and the pitcher contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of water, calculate the time required for the water in the pitcher to cool to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>28</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> from its original temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Neglect radiation effects. Latent heat of vapourization of water in this range of temperature is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>580</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and specific heat of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kcal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
As water equivalent of pitcher is 0.5 kg, i..e., pitcher is equivalent to 0.5 kg of water, heat to be extracted from the system of water and pitcher for decreasing its temperature from 30 to 28oC is

        Q 1 = m + M c Δ T

            = 9.5 + 0.5 kg  1 k cal/kg C ∘ 3 0 - 2 8 ∘ C

            = 2 0 kcal

And heat extracted from the pitcher through evaporation in t minutes

Q 2 = mL = dm dt × t L = 1 g min × t 5 8 0 cal g

                = 5 8 0 × t cal

According to given problem Q 2 = Q 1 ,  i.e., 5 8 0 × t = 2 0 × 1 0 3

                                          t = 34.5 min
